dnsGuide.currentKnown: Mail for {domain} arrives through {provider} today ({hosts}). Changing the MX sends all mail for any @{domain} address to MepMail Mail, and the {provider} mailboxes stop receiving. If you still use {provider}, put the MepMail Mail inboxes on a subdomain (e.g. correio.{domain}) or move every mailbox first.
dnsGuide.currentOther: The MX for {domain} points to {hosts} today. Changing it sends all of this domain's mail to MepMail Mail. If that server still receives mail you use, put the mailboxes on a subdomain (e.g. correio.{domain}).
dnsGuide.name: Name
dnsGuide.apexHint: @ is the domain itself. If the panel does not accept @, leave the name empty.

cloudflare.1: In Cloudflare, open the {zone} zone and go to DNS → Records → Add record.
cloudflare.2: Pick MX, name {name}, mail server {value} and priority 10. MX is never proxied, so there is no orange cloud.
cloudflare.3: Save and come back here to check.

registrobr.1: In Registro.br, sign in to the panel, open {zone} and choose Edit zone.
registrobr.2: New entry: type MX, name {name}, server {value}, priority 10.
registrobr.3: Save the zone. Registro.br can take a few minutes to publish it.

godaddy.1: In GoDaddy, open My domains → {zone} → DNS.
godaddy.2: Add new record: type MX, name {name}, value {value}, priority 10.
godaddy.3: Save and come back here to check.

route53.1: In AWS Route 53, open the {zone} hosted zone and click Create record.
route53.2: Record name {name} (empty for @), type MX, value {value}: the priority goes in front of it.
route53.3: Create the record and come back here to check.

hostinger.1: In Hostinger's hPanel, open Domains → {zone} → DNS / Nameservers.
hostinger.2: Add an MX record: name {name}, points to {value}, priority 10.
hostinger.3: Save and come back here to check.

locaweb.1: In the Locaweb panel, open the {zone} domain and its DNS editor.
locaweb.2: Add an MX record: name {name}, target {value}, priority 10.
locaweb.3: Save and come back here to check.

other.1: Open the panel where the DNS for {zone} is edited (whoever runs the nameservers {nameservers}).
other.2: Create an MX record: name {name}, value {value}, priority 10.
other.3: Save and come back here to check.

dnsGuide.removeOld: Once the MepMail MX record exists, delete the old MX records ({hosts}). With both in place, part of the mail keeps going to the old server and receiving is not confirmed.
dnsGuide.propagation: DNS changes usually show up within minutes, but can take a few hours.
